svg.text: Numbers are the order of these campaigns. 7 is one campaign. 8 is one campaign. Old lists of "17 raids" do not agree, so learn this order.
Dashed lines are classroom guides, not the exact path of each army. A defeat is one campaign. It does not always end the dynasty.

g.text: Temple town, not a dynasty capital
Temple city, on the Kannauj road

svg.text: Blue: north India. Brown word = Mahmud won that fight or took the spoil. The dynasty often went on.
Orange: Multan, the Thar, Somnath. Red word = he was stopped, or he did not keep the place.
Red road: Lohkot. Sangramaraja of Kashmir held it.
Dynasties: Ghaznavid 977-1186. Hindu Shahi, 9th century-1026. Ismaili Multan, about 959-1010. Gurjara-Pratihara, about 730-1036.

Chandela, 9th-13th century. Kachchhapaghata of Gwalior, 10th-12th century. Solanki (Chaulukya) of Gujarat, about 940-1244. Lohara of Kashmir from 1003. Tomaras at Delhi until the Chauhans in the 12th century.
He annexed the Punjab frontier and raided beyond it. Coastline: Natural Earth, public domain.
